extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians (researchers, graduate students), mathematical authors and evaluators
extracted.subtask_description: A checklist-style catalogue of dimensions on which mathematical work can be judged 'good', intended to guide self-evaluation, exposition, grant writing, and community valuation. Emphasizes that important work typically scores well on multiple dimensions rather than a single virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good mathematical problem-solving
rubrics_metrics.description: A major breakthrough on an important problem (e.g., Wiles on Fermat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values decisive solutions to central, long-standing problems; impact measured by importance of problem and novelty of resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good mathematical technique
rubrics_metrics.description: A masterful new way to compute, estimate, or manipulate (e.g., Stein's harmonic-analysis machinery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes development of methods and tools that make hard problems tractable; techniques may be reused across problems and fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good mathematical theory
rubrics_metrics.description: A conceptual framework that organizes many phenomena (e.g., Galois theory, scheme theory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values unifying theories that provide organization, perspective, and a foundation for further work across diverse examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good mathematical insight
rubrics_metrics.description: A single idea that suddenly clarifies an obscure subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small, illuminating ideas that change understanding or make problems transparent; often appear as key lemmas or viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good mathematical discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding an unexpected truth, phenomenon, or counter-example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewards uncovering phenomena or examples that reveal the landscape is different than previously believed, including counterexamples that correct misconceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good mathematical application
rubrics_metrics.description: Solving an external problem (physics, engineering, biology, CS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values work that bridges to other disciplines and provides real-world or cross-disciplinary solutions; impact measured by usefulness outside pure math.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good mathematical exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper, book, or talk that opens a field to outsiders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes clarity, accessibility, organization, and pedagogical generosity; expository work broadens the audience and lowers entry barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good mathematical pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Training future researchers; raising the technical level of a community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes mentoring, course materials, lectures and other activities that develop people and increase community capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good mathematical vision
rubrics_metrics.description: A long-range program that takes generations to complete (e.g., Langlands, Grothendieck).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values ambitious, programmatic directions that set agendas for entire fields and stimulate sustained development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good mathematical taste
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing the right problems, definitions, and abstractions; rejecting the wrong ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivates good judgment about what is important, natural, or productive to pursue; influences field evolution by focusing effort well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good mathematical public relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicating excitement and importance to non-specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values outreach and popularization that honestly conveys mathematics' significance without oversimplification; helps maintain public support and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good meta-mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Advances in foundations or in the philosophy of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes work on axiomatic frameworks, logical foundations, and conceptual analyses that clarify the nature and limits of mathematical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Airtight proofs with all details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritizes correctness and completeness of arguments; includes formal attention to definitions, hypotheses, and logical steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beautiful mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: A result whose statement and proof are aesthetically pleasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic value measured by simplicity, harmony, and conceptual neatness of statements and proofs; often subjective but widely recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elegant mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimal, surprising, and economical arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewards proofs or constructions that achieve more with less—concise, ingenious reasoning that avoids unnecessary complication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Genuinely novel constructions, not recombinations of known ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values originality of approach and invention of genuinely new objects or methods rather than routine extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Useful mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Feeds back into other parts of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures utility by the degree to which results, techniques, or concepts are adopted and used by other areas of mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharp constants, optimal exponents, best-possible bounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values quantitative strength and optimality; obtaining tight estimates or sharp thresholds is prized in many subfields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deep mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Penetrating to underlying causes (analogy, structure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterized by work that reveals structural reasons behind phenomena and connects superficially disparate facts through deeper principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intuitive mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Fits and extends naturally one's prior mental picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results that align with and extend intuition, offering conceptual understanding rather than merely technical results; aids human comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitive mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: The final word on a subject; closes a chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that settles a topic comprehensively, either by complete classification, definitive theorems, or closing major open directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-dimensionality and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Good mathematics is necessarily multi-dimensional; important results tend to satisfy several dimensions at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tao's central thesis: no single virtue suffices, and over the long run a healthy field needs contributions across many dimensions. Use the list as a checklist rather than a total ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks of optimizing a single dimension (failure modes)
rubrics_metrics.description: A field that optimizes only one dimension (only rigor, only applications, only beauty, only volume) will eventually decay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tao lists five failure modes to watch for: cynicism (pure technicality without meaning), isolation (cut off from neighboring fields), fragmentation (loss of shared taste/standards), exhaustion (running out of meaningful problems within a narrow focus), and irrelevance (losing broader significance). Use these as anti-patterns to avoid when valuing work.
